newsitem.title: USA: Calif. finance dept opposes bankruptcy legislation.
newsitem.headline: Calif. finance dept opposes bankruptcy legislation.

text.p: California's Department of Finance opposes legislation that would increase state oversight over local governments seeking bankruptcy protection, a department spokesman said on Monday.

Department of Finance Assistant Director H.D. Palmer said the department has expressed its opposition to the bill, which would require local agencies that intend to file for Federal bankruptcy protection to obtain approval from a state panel.
Governot Pete Wilson was expected to act on the measure by the end of September. Though his office declined to comment, sources said he was likely to veto the legislation.
Palmer said the department opposes the measure because it would "usurp" power from local elected officials.

The legislation, Senate Bill 349, would establish the Local Agency Bankruptcy Committee. Under the measure, local agencies that intend to file for bankruptcy would seek the committee's approval before petitioning the courts.
The committee would be comprised by the state Treasurer, the state Controller and the Director of the Department of Finance.
The measure was introduced in the wake of Orange County, Calif.,'s unprecedented bankruptcy filing.
Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion.
The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
Earlier this month, state Treasurer Matt Fong urged Wilson to sign the legislation.
"Before a local agency takes such a serious step as bankruptcy, that so dramatically affects the state, state level oversight should occur," Fong said.
